source.title: Taxonomizing local versus global structure in neural network loss landscapes
source.authors: Yaoqing Yang; Liam Hodgkinson; Ryan Theisen; Joe Zou; Joseph E. Gonzalez; K. Ramchandran; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: Sweeps ResNet18 width and other training conditions on image and translation tasks, measuring test accuracy and loss-landscape properties; this is a new setting relative to the listed version recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports width sweeps and correlations between test accuracy and loss-landscape measurements. It does not test fitting fully randomized labels, the specific one-hidden-layer ReLU setup, magnitude-aware sharpness, or the optimizer, dropout, and example-removal claims.
record.test_reason: The study reports width-dependent held-out performance, including explicitly identified width-wise double descent, in ResNet18 and Transformer settings. These results bear on V2 in new architectures and tasks. Connectivity and ordinary Hessian measurements alone do not test V2 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors associate the best held-out performance with globally well-connected, similar solutions in locally flat regions. They also find that approximately zero training loss can accompany worse held-out performance in poorly connected settings, and argue that local Hessian measurements alone are insufficient.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ResNet18 and other architectures with width, batch-size, data, and label-quality sweeps; it does not reproduce the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU width experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy and measured landscape properties vary with model width, batch size, learning rate schedule, weight decay, data quantity and quality, and dataset/architecture. Under linear learning-rate scaling, accuracy and landscape metrics change more slowly with batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width improves mode connectivity between independently trained networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider networks tend to have better-connected trained solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed width with noisy labels, locally flatter, approximately zero-loss models can have worse test accuracy than sharper models with higher training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinary Hessian flatness alone does not reliably predict held-out accuracy across these training conditions.

record.problems: The main accuracy and landscape sweeps are presented largely as figures without numerical values in the text. Results are averaged over five runs, but uncertainty intervals are not reported. Experiments omit data augmentation and the core versions' specific optimizer, dropout, and memorization interventions.
record.rows_left_out: No other eligible results were omitted. Many additional dataset, architecture, and temperature sweeps are figure-only; they were not added as separate rows because their numeric values cannot be recovered from the supplied text and they do not test another listed version.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fully randomized labels versus natural labels, including held-out accuracy at chance.
The original unregularized one-hidden-layer recipe is not reproduced. The supplied text does not locate the exact zero-training-error width or quantify a continuous improvement beyond it.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Batch sweeps use loss-based stopping with an epoch cap for image classification, and fixed gradient updates for translation; a common fixed epoch budget is not established.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: The explicitly reported width-wise double-descent result with 10% randomized labels, paired with training loss across widths. R1 records only a general phase-level accuracy association.

Transformer embedding-width versus held-out cross-entropy results explicitly described as width-wise double descent, with non-converged configurations distinguished. The generic declaration of omitted figure sweeps incorrectly dismisses their relevance to V2.
missing.locator: Appendix D.4; Figure 18a and caption; Appendix B.3

record.verdict_notes: The study is not a listed original source. V2 support is qualitative and based on explicit textual descriptions of double descent, not connectivity as a proxy. The fixed-width comparison in R3 cannot qualify the width claim. Exact plotted values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on fully randomized labels or report their held-out accuracy.

Uses ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 rather than one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; does not identify the interpolation threshold or compare test error immediately beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Batch size is varied, but the paper does not compare batches under a fixed epoch budget as specified.
Measures Hessian eigenvalues and trace, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, and does not compare that measure with norm- or margin-based measures as specified.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: Widths k, 2k, 4k, 8k across four major blocks; k varied
rows.operation_detail: Varied model width and measured test accuracy across batch-size settings on CIFAR-10.

conditions.value: standard setting; constant batch size, learning rate, and weight decay during each run

rows.value: The authors report that test accuracy improves after the mode-connectivity transition and is highest in Phase IV-B.
rows.uncertainty: Five independent runs averaged per configuration; no error bars stated.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative summary; precise accuracy values are shown only in the figure. The experiment does not isolate the width just beyond zero training error.
rows.check: The recorded phase-level accuracy summary does not establish whether additional width lowers test error after training error reaches zero. Record the width-wise performance and corresponding training fit instead. Appendix B.3 specifies loss-based stopping or a 150-epoch cap, SGD, and weight decay 5e-4.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: Widths k, 2k, 4k, 8k across four major blocks; k varied
rows.operation_detail: Varied model width and measured mode connectivity between independently trained models.
rows.value: The authors report that increasing model width improves connectivity.
rows.uncertainty: Five independent runs averaged per configuration; no error bars stated.
rows.note: This is a connectivity result, not itself a test-error result.
rows.check: Increasing mode connectivity with width is an observed landscape result, but it does not measure the held-out performance named by V2.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: Widths k, 2k, 4k, 8k across four major blocks; k varied
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian eigenvalue and trace alongside test accuracy across width and batch-size settings.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue and trace; test accuracy
rows.value: In a fixed-width slice through Phase III, the authors report that the best test accuracy is in Phase I/II, even though Phase III has smaller Hessian values and lower training loss.
rows.uncertainty: Five independent runs averaged per configuration; no error bars stated.
rows.note: This is evidence that ordinary local Hessian measures alone do not reliably track test accuracy in this setting; it does not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness named by V7.
rows.check: The reported Hessian–accuracy mismatch is supported by the text, but measures neither magnitude-aware sharpness in V7 nor the width intervention in V2. Remove its use as a V2 limits_scope verdict.
